meta.subtitle: From a mood board to a live website in one day. No coding experience needed.

starterPrompt.label: Step 10 · Claude starter prompt (copy exactly)
starterPrompt.text: This is my first time creating a website. Help me polish and finish the website design. I downloaded this from an online tool and would like to work on it locally until we have a final version. Familiarize yourself with the file, open it for me locally so I can see the changes, and let's work section by section from top to bottom, including the elements and anchor links. This is a single page website, static. Guide me through all this process.
starterPrompt.note: Word for word from the course outline. The only change is the apostrophe in "let's" (the outline has "lets").

workedExampleSpec.label: Worked example · Marisol's filled-in spec
workedExampleSpec.text:
Build a single-page, static website for… Piraguas de Marisol, my weekend piragua cart on Paseo de la Princesa in Old San Juan. Visitors should see the flavors and prices, know when and where to find the cart, and book it for their own events.

The section and layout are… Navbar (logo + links to Flavors, Where & When, Book the Cart). Hero (big photo of a rainbow piragua in front of the old city wall, headline "Shaved ice, the old San Juan way"). Flavors (four cards: Parcha, Frambuesa, Coco, Tamarindo, each with its price). Where & When (Saturday and Sunday, 11am to 5pm, Paseo de la Princesa, with a map). Book the Cart (office parties, birthdays and weddings, with a button that emails the business inbox). Kind Words (three short quotes from customers). Footer (Instagram and business email).

Use these colors and mood… #0B3C5D ocean, #FFF6E5 coconut, #FFB400 parcha, #FF5C8A frambuesa. Tropical, fresh and playful.

Extract and implement this element in the Hero section https://www.originkit.dev/ (the fade-up headline effect I saved)

slides.title: Build a website today with AI
slides.lead: Eleven steps, mostly free tools, and one very helpful ghost. Nothing to install until the last steps.
slides.body: Eleven simple steps, a handful of free tools, and one very helpful ghost. Nothing to install until the very last steps.
slides.try: Grab a laptop. We start right away.
slides.actionTip: Open your laptop. You will start collecting ideas right away.

stat.label: steps from idea to live website

slides.chloeLine: Boo! Don't worry, the only scary part today is how fast this goes.
slides.speakerNotes: Welcome everyone. The promise up front: nobody needs to know how to code. By the end you will know the full path from 'I like how this looks' to a real website with its own address, and you will be able to show someone else how to do it. The pixel ghost is Chloé, our course mascot. She'll pop up now and then.

slides.speakerNotes: Give the map before the journey. Steps 1 to 4 are gathering, like shopping for ingredients. Steps 5 and 6 are writing the recipe. Steps 7 to 10 are cooking. Step 11 is serving it.

slides.title: Collect
slides.lead: Images, animations, colors and your section order. Four places to look, one folder to fill.
slides.chloeLine: Collect first. I’m a professional hoarder.
slides.speakerNotes: Chapter 1, Collect (Steps 1-4). Four places to look: inspiration images, one or two animations, a color palette and your section order. Everything goes into one 'My Website' folder.
slides.layout: Full-bleed chapter slide (from Design A): one photograph, one giant word bleeding off the bottom edge, chapter tag 01 · Steps 1–4, dither wipe in, laser sweeps the word.

slides.title: Find inspiration images
slides.lead: Search for sites like yours. Screenshot the looks you love.
slides.body: Start on Pinterest. Search for the kind of site you want, take a screenshot of each look you love and save it in your 'My Website' folder.
bullets: Search terms that work: "shaved ice website", "food cart website", "tropical landing page"
Take a screenshot of each look you like
Save 2 or 3 images in your 'My Website' folder
Look for layout, mood and typography, not just pretty photos
Screenshot anything you like elsewhere, too
slides.try: Screenshot 3 looks. Save them in 'My Website'.
slides.actionTip: Take a screenshot of 3 looks you like and save the images in your 'My Website' folder.

ui.imageRule: Inspiration images must look like website designs (screens, layouts, UI), never lifestyle photos of people.

slides.chloeLine: Screenshot it! Ghosts never show up in photos.
slides.speakerNotes: Demo a quick search live if the Wi-Fi allows. Point out that we are looking for structure: where the headline sits, how big the photos are, how many sections. Two or three screenshots in the My Website folder is plenty, and it gives the AI a clearer signal later.
slides.imagePrompt: Six separate 3:4 and 4:5 website UI mockup images for a Pinterest-style search results grid, each a clean, realistic screenshot of a modern single-page website design (coffee roaster landing page, dark portfolio grid, restaurant menu, event landing page, mobile shop site on a phone, minimal studio site), varied palettes, placeholder text rendered as soft grey lines rather than words, no brand logos, crisp UI detail, 1600px on the long side or larger.

slides.title: Plan your sections
slides.lead: List your sections in order: Navbar first, then Hero, then the rest.
slides.body: List your website's sections in order. Always start with the Navbar at the top, then the Hero. After that, it is up to you.
bullets: 1. Navbar: logo and links
2. Hero: the big first impression, headline and button
Then add 3 or more: About, Services, Menu, Gallery, Reviews, Contact
Last: Footer with contact info and social links
Add one short idea per section, like 'three cards with photos'

slides.actionTip: Write your section list: Navbar, Hero, and at least three more, each with a one-line idea.

slides.chloeLine: Navbar first, Hero second. Even ghosts line up for the good stuff.
slides.speakerNotes: This is the most important thinking step. A website is just a stack of sections. Have people say their list out loud to a neighbor. This list gets pasted straight into the prompt in Step 5. Drag the cards on the slide to show that only the first two are fixed.

slides.title: Prompt
slides.lead: Turn everything you collected into one clear design spec.
slides.chloeLine: Now we turn your pile of ideas into one very clear wish.
slides.speakerNotes: Chapter 2, Prompt (Steps 5-6). Mash everything you collected into one design spec with the fill-in-the-blanks template, then let Bolt.new enhance it into a master prompt.

slides.title: Mash it into one design spec
slides.lead: Take what you like from every piece and describe it in one prompt.
slides.body: Take what you like from every inspiration piece and describe it in one prompt: mood from Pinterest, animations from OriginKit, colors from ColorHunt, layout from your list.

slides.speakerNotes: The key idea: you are the art director. The AI is fast, but it needs your taste. Mashing ideas from different sources is how you get something that doesn't look generic.

slides.chloeLine: Enhance! Like in the movies, but it actually works.
slides.speakerNotes: Sign in first (a free account works), then paste the notes. Two jobs here. First, the Enhance prompt button (click the + at the bottom-left of the box): it adds details about spacing, fonts and responsiveness. Save the enhanced version, that's your master prompt for every tool that follows. Second, press send: Bolt builds a design of its own from that prompt. Keep it; it's one of the five drafts you'll choose from in Step 8.
slides.notesExtra: Bolt needs a free account: sign in first, paste the spec, tap + and then "Enhance prompt".

Claude checks whether you have a GitHub account, walks you through creating a free one if not, then creates the repository, uploads the files, turns on GitHub Pages and hands you the live link. The first publish can take a moment; refresh the link if it isn’t up yet.
slides.notesExtra: Doing it by hand instead: make a new repository, upload the website folder (the main file must be named index.html), then Settings → Pages → Branch: main → Save.

slides.speakerNotes: Prices vary by name and ending, and the renewal price can differ from the first-year price, so check both. .com is not always the cheapest: endings like .site, .xyz, .party or .science are often cheaper and more fun. slides.notesExtra: Where to buy: Cloudflare or GoDaddy. "Enforce HTTPS" is the padlock switch in GitHub Pages settings.
